principle: Electrodeposits bond metallurgically only to atomically clean, oxide-free, active metal; every adhesion failure in gold plating traces to this chain, not to the gold bath. The chain removes three soil classes in order: organic (drawing lubricant/oil/fingerprints, removed by alkaline saponification+surfactant emulsification and O2/H2 gas-scrubbing during electrocleaning), inorganic oxide/scale (dissolved by acid pickle), and the self-healing passive film (on stainless, Cr2O3 reforms in seconds in air, so it must be removed AND overplated in the same instant — the Wood's nickel strike does both: high HCl content keeps the surface depassivated while low-efficiency Ni deposition with heavy H2 co-evolution lays a thin fresh nickel layer the next coat can bond to). A ductile barrier/underplate (Ni, Cu+Ni duplex, or nickel-free Pd/white-bronze) then blocks Fe/Cu interdiffusion into the thin gold, levels the surface, and carries corrosion protection so 0.5 um of gold does not have to. Rinse discipline between every tank prevents each chemistry from poisoning the next (drag-in) and precious-metal loss from the last (drag-out).

substrates: brass/copper/jeweler's bronze (skip pickle severity, cyanide- or non-cyanide-Cu-compatible)
steel houseware (spoons, cups) - same chain, bigger racks
aluminum houseware (different chain: zincate, out of scope here, flagged)
applicability.steel_wire_notes: As-drawn steel wire carries drawing lubricant (soap/stearate or oil) baked into the surface plus drawing oxide - the single most line-specific soil; soak-clean alone often fails on it, ultrasonic + anodic electroclean is the reliable combo. Mild steel: degrease -> electroclean (anodic) -> HCl pickle -> acid activation dip -> Cu or Ni strike -> Ni build -> Au. Stainless: degrease -> electroclean -> Wood's nickel strike (replaces pickle+activation, live entry) -> barrier -> Au. High-carbon/spring wire (owner's plate-then-form idea): pickle and cathodic steps charge hydrogen -> embrittlement -> wire snaps on coiling into rings; use anodic-only electrocleaning, inhibited short pickle, and a 190-220 degC 1-4 h bake within hours of plating if the wire is spring-tempered [FACT: published typical range, ASTM B850 class practice].
applicability.non_conductive_notes: This whole chain assumes a conductive metal substrate. Glass/ceramic houseware cannot enter it - they need prior metallization (electroless Ni/Cu seed, silvering, or conductive paint) or the PVD route; the pretreatment for THOSE is a different file. Plastic would need etch+catalyst (Pd/Sn) chains, out of scope.
applicability.jewelry_thickness_classes: The chain itself adds: strike 0.05-0.5 um, Ni underplate 1-5 um decorative (ISO 27874 / ASTM B488 practice puts a defined Ni or equivalent undercoat under thin gold classes; flash gold 0.05-0.175 um relies ENTIRELY on the undercoat for corrosion life; micron-class 1-2.5 um gold still specifies 1-5 um Ni beneath) [FACT: published typical range]. EU jewelry: nickel anywhere in the stack triggers EN 1811 release limits -> nickel-free stack (Cu strike -> white bronze or Pd) for allergy-safe skin contact [FACT: REACH Annex XVII entry 27 exists].

components.name: soak-clean tank (heated, PP or steel)
components.diy_notes: stainless stockpot or PP tank + sous-vide/aquarium-style heater with thermostat; lid to cut evaporation

components.name: ultrasonic cleaner 25-40 kHz
components.purpose: cavitation strips drawing lube from wire crevices
components.diy_notes: commodity 2-10 L ultrasonic benchtop units are cheap and genuinely effective; run with warm alkaline cleaner, not water alone

components.name: electrocleaning cell + DC rectifier
components.purpose: anodic (workpiece +) O2 gas-scrubbing of last soil monolayer; 3-10 A/dm2, 4-6 V
components.diy_notes: same adjustable bench PSU (0-15 V, 5-10 A) used for plating; steel cathode sheets; REVERSED polarity vs plating - wire is the ANODE here

components.name: pickle tank (PP/PVC only)
components.diy_notes: never metal-bodied; hardware-store muriatic acid (~31% HCl) diluted works; needs fume management - HCl fumes rust every tool in the room

components.name: activation dip tank
components.diy_notes: small beaker-scale is fine; the point is timing, not volume

components.name: Wood's nickel strike cell + Ni anode
components.purpose: simultaneous depassivation + Ni flash on stainless
components.diy_notes: small dedicated tank; rolled nickel anode sheet or Ni rounds in a titanium basket; MUST have live entry (current flowing before wire enters)

components.name: barrier plating tank(s) (Watts/sulfamate Ni, or Cu strike + white bronze/Pd)
components.purpose: 1-5 um ductile diffusion barrier under gold
components.diy_notes: heated, filtered (aquarium-pump + 5-10 um cartridge is the classic DIY filter), mild agitation; this is the biggest tank in the DIY line

components.name: counterflow rinse cascade (2-3 tanks) + dead rinse
components.purpose: drag-in/drag-out control; dead (static) rinse before the gold tank recovers gold value
components.diy_notes: three plastic tubs cascading beats one big rinse; a cheap conductivity (TDS) pen is the control instrument

components.name: DI/RO water source
components.purpose: final rinses and all bath make-up
components.diy_notes: aquarium RO/DI unit; tap-water chloride/calcium contaminates nickel and gold baths

components.name: fume extraction over acid/electroclean tanks
components.purpose: HCl fume, alkaline mist, H2 from strike
components.diy_notes: inline duct fan + hood to outdoors is the minimum; non-negotiable indoors

components.name: racks / reel-to-reel wire guides
components.purpose: hold work with electrical contact; for wire, guide pulleys + contact brushes through in-line cells
components.diy_notes: titanium or plastisol-coated copper hooks; for the owner's feed-through concept, the horizontal cell train clean-rinse-pickle-strike-plate-rinse-dry IS the industrial reel-to-reel answer and scales down

components.name: conductivity pen, pH strips/meter, thermometer, hydrometer (Baume)
components.diy_notes: under-100-USD instrument set controls the whole chain; titration kit is the upgrade

operation_sequence.action: Inspect + rack/reel wire; note steel grade (mild vs stainless vs spring) - it forks the chain at step 6
operation_sequence.parameters: electrical contact verified; wire spaced for solution access
operation_sequence.failure_watch: poor rack contact -> stepped/burned deposits later; misidentified stainless run as mild steel -> total adhesion failure

operation_sequence.parameters: 40-80 g/L builder cleaner, 50-80 degC; ultrasonic 25-40 kHz if available
operation_sequence.failure_watch: heavy drawing lube not lifting (extend time/temp); silicate cleaners leaving film if rinse is skimpy
alkaline drag-in neutralizing the pickle downstream

operation_sequence.parameters: 40-80 g/L alkaline electrocleaner, 60-80 degC, 3-10 A/dm2, 4-6 V
operation_sequence.failure_watch: cathodic mode on steel plates smut/metal film onto work; on spring steel cathodic mode also charges hydrogen; excessive anodic time on high-carbon steel raises smut

operation_sequence.action: Rinse + WATER-BREAK TEST: withdraw work, water must sheet unbroken >=30 s
operation_sequence.failure_watch: water beading anywhere = organics remain = STOP, return to step 2; this test gates the whole chain

operation_sequence.parameters: HCl 10-30 vol% ambient (or H2SO4 5-15 vol% at 60-70 degC), inhibitor added for spring/high-carbon wire
operation_sequence.duration: 1-5 min, shortest that gives uniform matte gray
operation_sequence.failure_watch: over-pickling -> pitting + hydrogen charging; black smut on high-carbon steel -> desmut dip needed; iron >~80-100 g/L in old HCl pickle -> dump [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]

operation_sequence.action: Rinse fast, then acid activation dip, then transfer WET and FAST to strike/plate
operation_sequence.parameters: 5-10% HCl or H2SO4 dip 15-60 s; transfer to next tank <30-60 s
operation_sequence.failure_watch: flash rust in air between tanks (visible orange bloom = re-pickle); any dry-out = adhesion risk

operation_sequence.action: STAINLESS PATH (replaces 6-7): Wood's nickel strike with LIVE ENTRY
operation_sequence.parameters: NiCl2.6H2O ~240 g/L + HCl ~120 mL/L, room temp, 3-10 A/dm2, current ON before immersion; optional 15-30 s brief anodic or acid pre-activation
operation_sequence.failure_watch: dead entry (no current at immersion) -> repassivation -> peeling; strike deposit dark/burned at high CD is normal-ish but powdery gray = too high; NO rinse-delay before next plate - transfer immediately or via quick acid-water rinse

operation_sequence.action: Strike layer for mild steel if going into acid baths: cyanide Cu strike OR non-cyanide alkaline Cu strike OR Ni strike
operation_sequence.parameters: low CD live entry, 0.5-2 A/dm2 class
operation_sequence.failure_watch: bare steel dipped straight into acid copper sulfate or acid gold gives immersion (displacement) deposit with ZERO adhesion - this is the classic beginner failure the strike exists to prevent

operation_sequence.action: Barrier/underplate build: Watts or sulfamate Ni (standard), or nickel-free stack (Cu strike -> white bronze Cu-Sn-Zn, or Pd) for EU-skin-contact jewelry
operation_sequence.parameters: see solutions; target 1-5 um decorative, sulfamate preferred if wire will be FORMED after plating (lowest stress, most ductile)
operation_sequence.duration: 5-30 min depending on CD and thickness
operation_sequence.failure_watch: pitting (needs wetter/agitation), high stress -> cracking on later bending, dull/burned edges at high CD

operation_sequence.action: Rinse cascade + dead rinse, conductivity-gated, then straight into gold strike/gold bath
operation_sequence.parameters: final rinse DI; rinse water conductivity before critical tank <~50 uS/cm [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]; dead rinse ahead of gold recovers drag-out
operation_sequence.failure_watch: nickel-bath drag-in is a listed poison of acid gold baths; chloride drag-in attacks some gold chemistries; never let nickel surface dry or sit passive >~10-30 min before gold - reactivate if delayed

operation_sequence.action: (Conditional) Post-plate hydrogen-embrittlement bake for spring-tempered/high-strength steel
operation_sequence.parameters: 190-220 degC, 1-4 h (up to 8-24 h for highest-strength classes), within 1-4 h of plating [FACT: published typical range, ASTM B850 class]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: skipping it on hard-drawn wire -> delayed brittle fracture when coiling rings days later; note bake also anneals some steels and can slightly color thin gold via diffusion - bake BEFORE gold when possible (after Ni, before Au) on embrittlement-critical parts

prep_chain_required: 1. Soak/ultrasonic alkaline degrease - WHY: organic soil blocks every later step; acids do not remove oil, they just pit under it
2. Rinse - WHY: alkaline drag-in neutralizes and gels (silicate) the pickle
3. Anodic electroclean - WHY: the last monolayer no soak removes; anodic polarity chosen to avoid smut plating and hydrogen charging on steel
4. Rinse + water-break test - WHY: the only free, instant, binary gate for cleanliness; failing work MUST go back, not forward
5a. (mild steel) HCl/H2SO4 pickle + activation dip - WHY: oxide prevents metallic bonding; the dip resets flash oxidation from the rinse
5b. (stainless / passive Ni) Wood's nickel strike, live entry - WHY: Cr2O3 repassivates in seconds; only simultaneous strip-and-deposit beats the clock
6. Strike layer before any acid plating bath on bare steel (Cu or Ni strike) - WHY: immersion/displacement deposition in acid baths gives zero-adhesion film

7. Barrier underplate 1-5 um (sulfamate Ni for form-after-plate; Watts bright Ni for level shine; Cu-strike+white-bronze or Pd for nickel-free) - WHY: Fe/Cu diffuse through thin gold and tarnish it; barrier also carries corrosion life so gold can stay thin (cost)
8. Cascade rinse + dead rinse + conductivity gate, wet transfer into gold - WHY: drag-in poisons gold baths (Ni2+, Cl-, cleaner), drag-out of gold is money; a passive-again nickel surface peels gold

deposit_properties.purity_karat: n/a for the chain itself (gold comes later); chain layers: Ni 99+%, Cu 99+%, white bronze alloy per bath, Pd 99+% or Pd-Ni 80/20
deposit_properties.hardness_HV: sulfamate Ni ~170-230 HV (additive-free); Watts semi-bright ~300-400 HV; bright (S-containing) Ni ~500-600 HV; white bronze ~450-600 HV class; Pd ~200-400 HV [FACT: published typical ranges, white bronze end [ESTIMATE]]
deposit_properties.thickness_per_pass: strike 0.05-0.5 um; underplate 1-5 um jewelry decorative; up to 10-25 um Cu leveling build if heavy polishing planned
deposit_properties.color_control: n/a underlayers except white bronze/Pd which read bright white and change perceived gold tone if gold is flash-thin (<0.2 um gold lets undercoat tint through) [FACT: known effect]
deposit_properties.ductility_forming_notes: CRITICAL for plate-then-form (owner Q3/Q5): stack ductility is set HERE, not by the gold. Ranking for post-plate bending: sulfamate Ni (near-zero stress, elongation up to ~10-30%) >> Watts semi-bright > bright Ni (sulfur-embrittled, cracks on sharp bends) > white bronze (hard, brittle). Duplex Cu(ductile)+thin sulfamate Ni is the friendliest mild-steel stack for coiling rings after plating. Hydrogen from pickle/cathodic steps embrittles spring wire independent of the coating - bake per step 12. Even ideal stacks: keep bend radius >= ~3-5x wire diameter or plate AFTER forming [ESTIMATE: practice-range, medium].

defects_and_remedies.defect: blistering/peeling of the whole stack (immediately or on bending)
defects_and_remedies.cause: soil or oxide under strike: failed water-break, dry-out between tanks, dead entry into strike, repassivated stainless
defects_and_remedies.remedy: gate on water-break; wet fast transfers; live entry; re-run Wood's strike with fresh HCl content

defects_and_remedies.defect: gold or Ni deposits with zero adhesion, dark, spongy
defects_and_remedies.cause: immersion (displacement) deposit - bare steel entered an acid metal bath without strike/current
defects_and_remedies.remedy: always strike first; live (hot) entry with current on

defects_and_remedies.defect: black/gray smut on steel after pickle or cathodic clean
defects_and_remedies.cause: carbon residue from high-carbon steel over-pickled; cathodic electroclean plate-out
defects_and_remedies.remedy: shorter inhibited pickle; desmut dip; use anodic electrocleaning

defects_and_remedies.cause: transfer delay >~60 s or acidic rinse left drying
defects_and_remedies.remedy: shorten transfers, activation dip just before strike, keep parts wet

defects_and_remedies.defect: wire snaps when coiled into rings days after plating
defects_and_remedies.cause: hydrogen embrittlement of spring/high-carbon wire from pickle + cathodic steps
defects_and_remedies.remedy: anodic-only cleaning, inhibited short pickle, 190-220 degC bake within hours of plating [FACT: published typical range]

defects_and_remedies.defect: gold bath performance decays after pretreatment upstream changes
defects_and_remedies.cause: drag-in: Ni2+, chloride, cleaner surfactants carried into gold
defects_and_remedies.remedy: add cascade stage + dead rinse, conductivity gate, longer drain times over tanks

defects_and_remedies.defect: adhesion fine flat, fails only at bends
defects_and_remedies.cause: brittle underplate (bright Ni or white bronze) or high internal stress
defects_and_remedies.remedy: switch to additive-free sulfamate Ni; increase bend radius; or form first, plate after

defects_and_remedies.defect: gel/haze film after cleaning, paint-like peeling later
defects_and_remedies.cause: silicate cleaner carry-over polymerizing in acid
defects_and_remedies.remedy: hot double rinse after silicated cleaners or use low/no-silicate cleaner before acid lines

defects_and_remedies.cause: H2 bubbles clinging (poor wetting/agitation), particulates, low boric
defects_and_remedies.remedy: wetter addition per TDS, filtration, agitation, boric acid replenish

defects_and_remedies.defect: stainless parts pass tape test, fail wrap test
defects_and_remedies.cause: partial repassivation - strike too weak (HCl depleted) or rinse delay strike-to-plate
defects_and_remedies.remedy: replenish strike HCl, no-rinse or instant transfer, verify with bend coupon each shift

cost_drivers: Chemicals are CHEAP here (NaOH, HCl, nickel salts) - the chain is <5-10% of consumable cost vs gold; skimping on it destroys 100% of the gold value via rework [ESTIMATE: cost-structure, high]
Nickel salt price and Ni anode metal (LME nickel exposure) for underplate volume
Nickel-free premium: Pd flash is PGM-priced (grams matter); white bronze proprietary systems carry supplier margin + analysis service
Water: counterflow rinsing cuts water 10-100x vs single overflow rinse - dominant utility saving [FACT: standard rinse-ratio math]
Waste disposal: spent pickle liquor, nickel-bearing sludge, (any) cyanide destruct - permitted-disposal cost can exceed chemical purchase cost at small scale
Labor/time: the chain is ~10-20 min per load regardless of load size - batching and reel-to-reel amortize it
Rework rate is THE hidden driver: every adhesion failure costs strip+replate of gold

hazards: HCl: corrosive, fuming - burns, respiratory irritation [FACT]
H2SO4: corrosive, exothermic dilution (always acid INTO water) [FACT]
Nickel chloride/sulfate/sulfamate: skin sensitizer cat.1, carcinogen cat.1A for inhalable Ni compounds (mist from air agitation!), aquatic chronic 1 [FACT]
Boric acid: reprotoxic 1B under EU CLP [FACT]
Copper/sodium cyanide (if cyanide strike used): acute tox., liberates FATAL HCN gas on ANY acid contact - segregation of cyanide and acid lines is life-critical [FACT]
Hydrogen gas from strike/cathodic steps: flammable accumulation under lids/foam blankets [FACT]
Hydrogen embrittlement: delayed mechanical failure hazard of finished spring-steel product [FACT]
controls: Fume extraction over acid + electroclean tanks; lids when idle
PPE: goggles/face shield, chemical gauntlets, apron, boots; eyewash + shower within reach
Physical + drainage segregation of cyanide from all acids (separate room/spill path if cyanide is used at all; DIY: choose cyanide-free routes and delete the hazard)
No air agitation of nickel baths without mist control (Ni carc. classification is inhalation-driven) - use eductor/cathode-rod agitation at DIY scale
SDS-driven storage: acids cabinet separate from alkalis, cyanides (if any) locked and separate
Post-plate embrittlement bake procedure written into the traveler for spring wire
safety.waste: Segregate streams: (1) acid/alkali rinses - neutralize to pH 6-9, precipitate heavy metals as hydroxides, filter sludge (nickel-bearing sludge = hazardous waste class) [FACT: standard treatment]; (2) spent pickle liquor - licensed disposal; (3) cyanide-bearing (if any) - alkaline chlorination destruct BEFORE it can ever meet acid; (4) dead-rinse gold-bearing water - send to gold recovery, it is revenue not waste. Local discharge permits govern - [UNKNOWN — jurisdiction-specific limits, needs local check].

diy_feasibility.verdict: HIGH - this is the most DIY-feasible family in the whole project, and also the most consequential: a garage line that nails pretreatment will outperform a sloppy pro line. Every solution except white bronze and Pd can be home-mixed from commodity chemicals to published recipes.
diy_feasibility.minimum_viable_setup: 6-8 plastic tanks/tubs (2-10 L), one 0-15 V/10 A bench PSU (shared: electroclean reversed, strike, plate), commodity ultrasonic cleaner, aquarium heaters + RO/DI unit, conductivity pen + pH strips + thermometer, duct-fan fume hood, Ni anode sheet, chemicals: NaOH/metasilicate/carbonate cleaner, muriatic acid, NiCl2+HCl (Wood's), Ni sulfamate or Watts salts, boric acid. Budget class: low hundreds of USD excluding the gold bath [ESTIMATE: component-price class, medium]. Skip cyanide copper entirely - route mild steel via Ni strike or buy a non-cyanide Cu strike.
diy_feasibility.hard_limits: (1) Nickel exposure: sensitizer/carcinogen - not a kitchen activity; dedicated ventilated space, gloves discipline, or you WILL develop nickel allergy; (2) EU/skin-contact nickel-free stacks (white bronze, Pd) are proprietary-TDS territory - buy the system, don't home-brew; (3) waste: you cannot pour nickel or spent pickle down a drain legally - small-scale licensed disposal or evaporation-to-solid + hazardous-waste drop-off must be planned before the first liter is mixed; (4) analysis: beyond hobby volume, baths need titration/AAS service - white bronze especially; (5) hydrogen-embrittlement bake needs a temperature-controlled oven if spring wire is used.
